title: Canonical truncation filtration and shifted cohomology graded pieces
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $K^n=0$ outside a finite interval. Define a decreasing filtration by good upper truncations $F^iK=\tau_{\le -i}K$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, def-sp-filtration]. Then $F^aK=K$ and $F^bK=0$ for suitable integers $a<b$, so $(K,F)$ is a finite filtered complex [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. For every $i$, the quotient $F^iK/F^{i+1}K$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] is the two-term complex $\operatorname{im}(d^{-i-1})\hookrightarrow\ker(d^{-i})$ in degrees $-i-1,-i$, and the projection of cycles induces a natural quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] $F^iK/F^{i+1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{-i}(K)[i]$. These comparisons are natural for chain maps [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and a chain homotopy [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] between chain maps induces a filtration-preserving chain homotopy between their truncation maps. Consequently a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] $K\to L$ induces a quasi-isomorphism on every graded quotient.
